requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Discovery confirmed appworker did not exist (id: no such user), then useradd -m created it with uid/gid 1000, confirmed by id output. Account persisted after the subsequent reboot.

requirements.requirement: Login sessions for appworker limited to 8,192 open files
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nofile 8192; a real login shell (su -l appworker) confirmed ulimit -n returns 8192 both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Login sessions for appworker limited to 256 processes
requirements.summary: Same config file sets soft/hard nproc 256; su -l appworker verification returned ulimit -u = 256 both before and after reboot.

overall_summary: The executor created the appworker account on node1 and configured /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with nofile 8192 and nproc 256 for both soft and hard limits, verifying the effective limits via a real login shell (su -l) both before and after a full reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly: pre-restart boot_id and healthy state were captured, the reboot was acknowledged, connectivity was lost during the transition, and a distinct post-restart boot_id confirmed a genuine restart with the account and limits intact afterward, cross-checked by the fixed before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: No independent verification was performed of pam_limits.so being active in the su/login PAM stack beyond the observed effective ulimit values, though the su -l test is a reasonably direct behavioral proof.
A small /tmp/reboot.log artifact remains from the backgrounded reboot command; low-risk but not cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map to a clear purpose: discovery (cmd-d1e7e4bca1af41a6), account creation (cmd-0c64f99ff3614666), limits config write (cmd-17cd4ba16dd74664), and the mandated provider-wide restart evidence protocol (cmd-6226b0a74b8e4caa reboot, with pre/post baseline captures). No troubleshooting dead-ends or unrelated mutations were found. The only residue is a small /tmp/reboot.log created as a byproduct of the backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' redirection (visible in after_executor:node1:temporary-files); this is low-risk, bounded, and a routine artifact of the mandated restart protocol rather than an unnecessary mutation, but it was left in place rather than cleaned up.
